name: Cell Project Space
summary: An artist-founded gallery on Cambridge Heath Road, started in 1999 and at its current Bethnal Green site since 2003. A ground-floor event space was added in the summer of 2019.

accessibility.notes: Level access to the entrance through a courtyard gate; ring to be let in. The gallery is on the first floor, with a wheelchair lift and staff to help. Shallow ramps lead into the ground-floor event space. The nearest accessible toilet is about 100 metres away at the Museum of Childhood.

evidence.quote: Founded in 1999, Cell Project Space was built by artists Milika Muritu & Richard Priestley
In 2003, the gallery and HQ relocated to our current Bethnal Green site, on Cambridge Heath Rd
a recent new addition of a ground-floor multi-purpose event space, opened in the summer 2019
Cell Project Space Gallery is situated on the first floor and has a wheelchair lift for use by visitors.
there are no wheelchair accessible toilets in the building
There is level access to the main entrance of Cell Project Space
To access the courtyard, please ring at the gate and we will open the gate for wheelchair access.
There are shallow ramps inside the yard, into the reading room, gallery office and the ground floor event space (all are wheelchair accessible).
there is a fully accessible toilet available in The Museum of Childhood 100 metres from the gallery on Cambridge Heath Road
Cell Project Space is committed to being open and accessible to all.
